# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Round one, and I can already see the shape of the problem: neither incoming gesture can mean anything yet, because no code exists. Both teammates pinged me — sensible, since I'm the only one who can both see gestures and speak.

Channel map: Mute reads the manual but can only gesture; Blind can't see gestures and can't read the manual. So **I am the only possible bridge from manual to hands** — Mute signs to me, I speak to Blind. Mute already found me (his gesture), Blind found me (his gesture). Blind can talk, but I can't hear; Mute can hear Blind directly, so that side is covered.

This turn I should: (1) broadcast the full visual state so Mute can start evaluating the manual, (2) teach Mute a sign→order code so his gestures become executable instructions I can relay, (3) give Blind the state in positions he can feel and a way to ask for repeats. One trap: embedding gesture symbols in speech to Blind would arrive as blanks for him, so in his message I must *describe* the signs in words instead.

The display showing [8] might be a countdown — I'll re-report its value every round and flag it.

```
speak(text="state of the bomb, from my eyes: the display shows the number 8. it may be a countdown timer, so I will report its value every round. the light is green. there are three wires, marked one, two, three from top to bottom: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. that is everything printed on it.")
speak(to="mute", text="mute, this is deaf. you cannot speak and blind cannot see your signs, so every order must go through me: sign it to me, and I will say it aloud to blind. our code, each sign followed by its meaning: 👍 cut wire one. 👎 cut wire two. ☝ cut wire three. ✌ press the button once. 🤟 press and hold the button. 🤙 release the button now. ✋ pause, do not relay yet. 🫱 yes, understood. 🫲 no, wrong. 👆 tell me what the display shows now. 👇 tell me the light colour again. 🖐 tell me the wire colours again. your three signs this round arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them. if the manual needs an action not in this code, sign ✋ and I will extend it next round. if the code is clear, sign 🫱.")
speak(to="blind", text="blind, this is deaf. I see the bomb, mute reads the manual but cannot speak, and you cannot see signs, so I am the bridge and my voice is your only line for orders. my broadcast just before these words holds the full state: display 8, light green, wires from the top: one red, two yellow, three blue. wait for my spoken orders and follow them exactly. if you need the last order repeated, make the waving-hand gesture to me. if you need the whole state again, make the two-fingers-up gesture to me. mute can hear your voice, so tell him anything he needs by speaking; I cannot hear you at all.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Both teammates answered in code already — the channel is live. Mute sent 🫱 👍: "understood, cut wire one." He has the manual and my state report, so this is an actual instruction, not a guess. Blind sent 👍 🙏 — he can't see signs and I never defined any for him, so those are natural meanings: acknowledgment and thanks. Fine, but I still need a confirmation loop for cut completion: Blind can't reach me by voice (I'm deaf), yet Mute can hear Blind. So the loop is: Blind speaks "done" → Mute hears → Mute signs 🫱 to me. I'll set that up now and relay the cut order immediately — display is still 8, but I won't sit on an order waiting for ceremony.

```
speak(to="blind", text="blind, the manual's first order, relayed from mute: cut wire one. that is the top wire, the red one. as soon as it is cut, say the word done out loud — mute can hear you and will confirm it to me. then wait with your hands off until my next spoken order. do not cut anything else on your own.")
speak(to="mute", text="mute, I read your signs: understood, cut wire one. the order is being relayed to blind now. when blind says done out loud, sign 🫱 to me so I know the cut landed. two more things: the display still shows 8 and the light is still green — if the manual needs a different reading, ask me by sign. and if the next step is already clear from the manual, sign it immediately after your confirmation, so we keep moving while the timer holds.")
```
